summary: Festival EDM (big room, progressive house, electro house): 126-130 BPM four-on-the-floor with big claps and snare-roll builds, a pumping saw bass, wide supersaw chords and a bright supersaw lead hook in the drop, everything sidechained; knowledge/style/edm.json is its template
body: Drums: a hard, short four-on-the-floor kick, big layered 909 claps (or clap and snare) on 2 and 4, off-beat open hats and a shaker; builds with snare rolls doubling in speed toward the drop, a crash on its first beat; the drop strips to kick and hook, the breakdown drops the kick.
Bass: a saw or FM bass on the chord roots, off-beat or 8ths, a sine sub under it; ducked hard by the kick (the sidechain pump is the genre's sound).

Harmony: pop progressions in minor keys: I-V-vi-IV, i-III-VII-VI ('Levels'), i-VI-VII, vi-IV-I-V; piano chords in the breakdown, wide supersaw or polysynth chords held through the drop, pumping with the sidechain.
Lead: the supersaw: stacked detuned saws (unison), bright, high-passed, with a long pre-delayed reverb; plays the hook high, layered in octaves; the breakdown's melody becomes the drop lead.
Texture/master: loud, wide and bright; everything sidechained to the kick, reverbs filtered, hard limiting for festival loudness.

Sources (2026-11-26): Native Instruments 'EDM chord progressions' and 'Progressive house'; EDMProd 'How To Make House Music' (big room sidechain); Syntorial 'Crafting the supersaw EDM lead'; LANDR 'How to make EDM'; MusicRadar '10 ways to create monstrous big room synth sounds'.
Apply: pattern/four-on-the-floor on the drums, then pattern/prog-edm-common-1 on the keys four bars later. For a whole style change the Team Lead's restyle uses knowledge/style/edm.json instead.

drums.about: the drum track (a kit); leave out if there isn't one

keys.about: a chordal part (keys, pad); leave out if there isn't one

key.about: the project's key; leave out to estimate it from the notes
